1001504.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Nanna, the name of a goddess in Norse mythology. The deeper origin of the Old Norse name is uncertain. One traditional analysis connects it with a name element from Proto-Germanic *nanþ- (“bold, daring”), related to *ninþaną (“to dare, venture”). The latter is ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *nant- (“to fight, dare”).
Another proposal connects the Old Norse name with a nursery-language word for “mother”, comparable to similar nanna-type kinship words.

1004832.etyen:
From hanske (“glove”) + -makeri (“activity- or workshop-forming suffix”), literally “glove-making activity or workshop”; compare hanskemaker (“glovemaker”). The suffix -makeri (“activity- or workshop-forming suffix”) is from Middle Low German -makerie, from maken (“to make, do”).
Compare Danish handskemageri (“glovemaking”).

1005088.etyen:
PIE word
 *stéh₂tis
Inherited from Old Norse *Bjúgsstaðir (“Bjúgr's farmsteads”), from the genitive singular Bjúgs of the male personal name Bjúgr + staðir (“places, farmsteads”), the plural of staðr (“place, stead”), literally “Bjúgr's farmsteads”.
First attested in 1360, in the surviving manuscript of Bergens kalvskinn in the locative form of Middle Norwegian Biugstodhuni.
The second element staðr is from Proto-Germanic *stadiz (“place, location”), from Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂tis (“standing, position”), from the root *steh₂- (“to stand”).
